scenario: A young woman, a final-year student, cannot sleep and is afraid of failing her exams; she feels her family's hopes are heavy. No thoughts of self-harm.

transcript.text: Hello. Please tell me, what's on your mind today?
Hello. I'm just feeling very stressed, you know. My final exams are coming up, and I can't sleep at all.
So, you're feeling a lot of stress and anxiety about your upcoming exams, and it's even affecting your sleep.
Yes, exactly. And my family has so many hopes from me. It feels like such a heavy burden.
It sounds like you're carrying a lot of your family's expectations. Can you tell me more about what that feels like?
It's like I cannot afford to fail. Everyone is expecting me to do well, to get a good job. I just feel so much pressure.
You're feeling an immense pressure, almost like a fear of letting everyone down if you don't meet their high expectations.
Absolutely. It's constantly on my mind, day and night. That's why I just can't switch off and sleep.
Have you tried maybe doing some meditation or listening to calming music before bed? That often helps with sleep.
I've tried a bit, but my mind just keeps racing. It's hard to focus on anything else when I'm so worried about the results.
So, are you saying you feel completely stuck and helpless right now?
Yes, in a way. I just don't know how to handle all this pressure.

cards.opening: You spent time understanding the weight of the client's family expectations and how they contribute to his exam stress. I noticed how carefully you listened to his feelings of being overwhelmed.

what_worked.quote: So, you're feeling a lot of stress and anxiety about your upcoming exams, and it's even affecting your sleep.
what_worked.lead: You acknowledged his stress early on.
what_worked.body: By repeating back his struggle with sleep and exams, you showed him that you were truly listening and understood the immediate problem he was facing.

what_worked.quote: You're feeling an immense pressure, almost like a fear of letting everyone down if you don't meet their high expectations.
what_worked.lead: You uncovered the source of his burden.
what_worked.body: Moving beyond the exams to identify his fear of letting his family down helped deepen the conversation and allowed him to share more about his inner thoughts.

work_on_this.quote: Have you tried maybe doing some meditation or listening to calming music before bed? That often helps with sleep.
work_on_this.lead: Focus on staying with the feeling longer.
work_on_this.why: Suggesting solutions like meditation too early can sometimes make a person feel like their deeper distress is being overlooked or fixed too quickly.
work_on_this.try_saying: I can see how much these results are weighing on you, tell me more about what happens when you try to rest.

practise_next.reason: Continuing to explore the client's feelings before moving into problem-solving helps build a stronger connection and ensures the person feels fully heard.

cards.reflective_question: What do you think would happen if you spent more time exploring the client's feelings of helplessness before suggesting ways to cope?
